_comment: Config for the weekly sharded mutation run.
SCOPE: RunnerCore + Core, graded by CoreTests. Worker is NOT in the sweep, and
that is a retreat from evidence rather than an oversight. Run 2 aborted on all
ten shards because Muter's BASELINE suite failed -- `Suite WorkerTests failed
with 2 issues` -- and Muter refuses to mutate anything when the unmutated suite
is red. WorkerTests carries the timing-sensitive sandbox and timeout tests
(scriptTimesOut, scriptTimeoutReapsBackgroundChildProcess) and spawns concurrent
worker daemons; running it in ONE process alongside CoreTests, on a 2-core
runner, is a configuration nothing else exercises -- CI runs those targets as
separate jobs, and on a laptop the interpreter-dependent tests skip. Re-adding
Worker needs that instability understood first, not a bigger timeout.
COST at this scope: ~10.2k LOC, ~1,700 mutants at one per 6 lines, ~16s each,
so ~7.5h serial and ~45 min per shard across 8.
APIServer stays out permanently: 94k LOC, ~15,700 mutants that must be graded by
APITests, ~1,712h serial -- ~96% of the tree's cost for its least informative
mutants (route wiring, Leaf, Fluent models). Triage cost scales with SURVIVORS,
and a report nobody can read is worse than none because it looks like coverage.
KNOWN CAVEAT, stated rather than hidden: some Core code is reached only through
APITests, which this command does not run. Mutants covered solely there will
survive and read as holes that are not real. Verify a survivor by hand before
writing a test for it -- which the report already tells the reader to do.
--skip ZipProcessEnvironmentTests IS REQUIRED. Muter writes a preamble into
every file it will mutate -- including `import class Foundation.ProcessInfo` --
BEFORE running the baseline. That suite reads Sources/Core/ZipArchiver.swift and
ZipProcessSerialization.swift and scans them for `Process(` constructions, so the
preamble trips it. The general rule: a test asserting on the TEXT of a file under
mutation cannot coexist with mutation, and has no mutants worth killing anyway.
-Xswiftc -no-warnings-as-errors IS LOAD-BEARING. The package builds with
.treatAllWarnings(as: .error), and RemoveSideEffects deletes the USE of a
binding, leaving `let x = ...` unused -- a warning, therefore an error, therefore
a copy that does not compile and a shard that produces zero mutants.
